project.name: E-Commerce Platform
project.summary: Online marketplace for customers to browse, purchase, and track orders, with seller product management and admin oversight.

functional_requirements: Customers can browse the product catalogue
Customers can add products to a shopping cart
Customers can checkout and pay online
Sellers can list products and manage inventory
Administrators can approve sellers and process refund requests
non_functional_requirements: The system must enforce secure authentication and data encryption
The platform must scale to support high concurrent user traffic
Response time for user actions should be under 2 seconds

actors.name: Customer
actors.description: Browses products, adds items to cart, makes purchases, and tracks orders

actors.name: Seller
actors.description: Lists products, updates inventory, and fulfills orders after approval

actors.name: Administrator
actors.description: Approves seller registrations, manages refunds, and oversees platform governance

use_cases.name: Browse Catalogue
use_cases.description: Customer searches and views product listings

use_cases.name: Add to Cart
use_cases.description: Customer selects products and adds them to a shopping cart

use_cases.name: Checkout and Pay
use_cases.description: Customer completes payment using an online payment gateway

use_cases.name: List and Manage Products
use_cases.description: Seller creates product entries and updates stock levels

use_cases.name: Approve Seller and Process Refund
use_cases.description: Administrator reviews seller applications and handles customer refund requests

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Customers can browse the product catalogue
criteria: Search results return relevant products within 1 second
Product details page displays price, images, and description

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Customers can add products to a shopping cart
criteria: Item appears in cart immediately after selection
Cart persists across user sessions

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Customers can checkout and pay online
criteria: Payment gateway processes transactions with success rate ≥ 99.5%
Order confirmation email is sent within 30 seconds

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Sellers can list products and manage inventory
criteria: Seller can create a product listing in under 2 minutes
Inventory updates reflect in catalogue within 5 seconds

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Administrators can approve sellers and process refund requests
criteria: Seller approval workflow completes within 24 hours
Refunds are issued and notified to customers within 48 hours

user_stories.story: As a customer, I want to browse the product catalogue, so that I can find items to purchase.
acceptance_criteria: The catalogue displays product name, image, price, and stock status.
Customers can filter and search products by category, name, or price.

user_stories.story: As a customer, I want to add products to a shopping cart, so that I can purchase multiple items in one order.
acceptance_criteria: Items can be added, updated quantity, or removed from the cart.
Cart contents persist across user sessions until checkout or explicit clearing.

user_stories.story: As a customer, I want to pay online securely, so that my transaction is safe and completed quickly.
acceptance_criteria: Payment gateway supports credit/debit cards and tokenized payment methods.
Sensitive data is encrypted in transit and not stored in plain text.

user_stories.story: As a seller, I want to list new products after approval, so that I can start selling them on the platform.
acceptance_criteria: Approved sellers can create product entries with title, description, price, and inventory.
New listings become visible to customers only after successful admin approval.

user_stories.story: As an administrator, I want to approve seller accounts, so that only vetted sellers can list products.
acceptance_criteria: Admin can view pending seller applications and approve or reject them.
Rejected sellers receive a notification with the reason for rejection.

user_stories.story: As an administrator, I want to handle refund requests, so that customers receive timely reimbursements.
acceptance_criteria: Admin can view, approve, or deny refund requests with status updates.
Approved refunds trigger an automatic notification to the customer and update order status.

    C->>UI: Add product to cart

    UI->>OS: CreateOrder(cartId)

    C->>UI: Track order
    UI->>OS: GetOrderStatus(orderId)
    OS-->>UI: status

A user can place many orders

Database Designer.sql:
CREATE TABLE users (
    user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT,
    email TEXT,
    password_hash TEXT,
    is_admin BOOLEAN
);

CREATE TABLE sellers (
    seller_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    user_id INTEGER,
    store_name TEXT,
    approved BOOLEAN,
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE products (
    product_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    seller_id INTEGER,
    name TEXT,
    description TEXT,
    price REAL,
    stock INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (seller_id) REFERENCES sellers(seller_id)
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
    order_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    user_id INTEGER,
    order_date DATETIME,
    total_amount REAL,
    status TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(user_id)
);

apis.purpose: Retrieve a list of available products with optional filters
Add a product to the customer's shopping cart
Create an order and process payment
Retrieve order details and tracking information
Update the status of a refund request

Project Structure.architecture: Micro‑service style with a single FastAPI service handling authentication, product, cart, order and admin APIs. React/Vite SPA consumes these APIs. PostgreSQL stores relational data; Redis provides session caching and async task queue (Celery). Nginx terminates TLS and load‑balances multiple Docker containers. CI/CD pipelines automate testing, container builds and deployments.
Project Structure.architecture_diagram:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Client
        A[React SPA] -->|REST/GraphQL| B[FastAPI Gateway]
    end
    subgraph Backend
        B --> C[Auth Service]
        B --> D[Product Service]
        B --> E[Cart Service]
        B --> F[Order Service]
        B --> G[Admin Service]
        D --> H[PostgreSQL]
        E --> H
        F --> H
        G --> H
        F --> I[Redis Cache]
        F --> J[Celery Workers]
        J --> K[RabbitMQ]
    end
    subgraph Infra
        L[Nginx] --> B
        M[Docker Compose]
        L --> M
    end

Documentation.readme: E‑Commerce Platform: customers browse catalog, add to cart, checkout, track orders. Sellers list products, manage inventory after admin approval. Admins approve sellers, handle refunds. Built with React frontend, Node.js/Express API, PostgreSQL DB, Stripe for payments, JWT auth. Emphasizes security, scalability, performance.
Documentation.api_documentation: POST /auth/login – JWT token. POST /auth/register – user role (customer/seller). GET /products – list with filters. GET /products/:id – details. POST /cart – add item. GET /cart – view. POST /checkout – Stripe payment, create order. GET /orders – customer orders. POST /sellers – create product (admin approved). PUT /sellers/:id/inventory – update stock. POST /admin/approve-seller – approve. POST /admin/refund – process refund.
Documentation.installation: Clone repo, run `npm install` in both client and server directories. Set env vars: DB_URL, JWT_SECRET, STRIPE_KEY. Initialize PostgreSQL schema with provided migrations. Run `npm run dev` for development.
Documentation.deployment: Containerize with Docker. Use Docker Compose for app, DB, and Redis cache. Deploy to Kubernetes or cloud VM. Configure HTTPS via Let’s Encrypt. Enable auto‑scaling and health checks.
Documentation.sprint_plan: Sprint 1: Core user auth, product catalog API. Sprint 2: Cart, checkout, Stripe integration. Sprint 3: Seller onboarding, inventory management. Sprint 4: Admin approval workflow, refund handling. Sprint 5: Performance tuning, security hardening, CI/CD pipeline.
Documentation.architecture: Frontend: React SPA with Redux. Backend: Node.js/Express REST API, JWT auth, role‑based access. DB: PostgreSQL for relational data, Redis for session cache. Payments: Stripe. Messaging: RabbitMQ for async order processing. Deployed on Docker/K8s with load balancer.
